{{Short description|British chemical physicist}}
{{distinguish|text = [[David K. Smith]], professor of chemistry at the University of York}}
'''David Smith''' {{postnominals|FRS}}<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Španěl |first1=Patrik |last2=Risby |first2=Terence H. |date=2024 |title=David Smith. 26 November 1935—15 February 2023 |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2024.0013 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=77|pages=335–351 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2024.0013 |doi-access=free }}</ref> (26 November 1935—15 February 2023) was a British [[Chemical physics|chemical physicist]] who investigated [[Gas-phase ion chemistry|gas-phase ionic reactions]] between ions, electrons and molecules. For this work he developed the selected ion flow tube (SIFT) technique, an analytical method that evolved in to the widely used [[Selected-ion flow-tube mass spectrometry|SIFT-mass spectrometry]].
== Career ==
In 1991, he took up a professorship at the [[University of Innsbruck|Innsbruck University]] Institute for Ion Physics, and returned to the UK in 1996, returning to Keele University, where he would remain until retirement in 2016. His work continued though with collaboration with the [[Czech Academy of Sciences|J. Heyrovský Institute of Physical Chemistry]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023 |title=Professor David Smith, FRS passed away |url=https://www.jh-inst.cas.cz/index.php/news/professor-david-smith-frs-passed-away}}</ref> in Prague.

He was a Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Španěl |first1=Patrik |last2=Risby |first2=Terence H |date=2023 |title=Obituary: Professor David Smith |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1752-7163/acca3d |journal=Journal of Breath Research |volume=17 |issue=3|page=030401 |doi=10.1088/1752-7163/acca3d |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
